topic: How do GEO satellite propagation delays influence link budget margins for latency-sensitive applications?
consensus_response: GEO satellite propagation delays significantly impact link budget margins for latency-sensitive applications. The fixed latency of 250-300 ms due to signal travel time negatively affects TCP throughput, as congestion control mechanisms rely on Round-Trip Time (RTT). To mitigate this, adopting layer 2 operation in satellite backhaul networks can reduce latency. However, this may require additional infrastructure investments to compensate for increased link utilization and capacity requirements. Moreover, longer delay windows require more robust forward error correction (FEC) coding, increasing overhead and complexity.
reference_context: GEO satellites operate at a height of approximately 36,000 km, resulting in fixed latency on satellite links in the order of magnitude of a few hundred milliseconds, negatively impacting QoS and applications that are not tolerant against high latencies.
